metric_audit.experiment_03_impact: Published precision/recall pair counts are arithmetically correct. The field named false_positive_rate measured only synthetic negative-query acceptance, so it did not describe the 4,394 incorrect positive-query pairs. Experiment 04 adds pair FPR and query-with-FP rate; Experiment 03 files remain unchanged.
metric_audit.pair_rule: one query-candidate decision; the ground-truth candidate is the sole positive
metric_audit.recall_denominator: positive queries (one expected pair per query)
metric_audit.query_fpr_denominator: positive queries; event is at least one incorrect confirmation
metric_audit.multiple_false_confirmations: counted individually for pair precision/FPR and once for query FPR
metric_audit.experiment_03_ranking: ORB: descending (inliers, inlier ratio, filtered matches, negative median distance), lexical path tie-break. Union: ascending pHash rank first, ORB rank second; therefore pHash dominated ordering even when it had poor Strong retrieval.

partition.caveat: Strong test identities were reported in Experiment 03 and are not a prospectively unseen benchmark. They were not used to select Experiment 04 thresholds. Natural evaluation pairs and distractors are identity-disjoint from calibration. The final database contains only its held-out distractor half, so absolute results are not directly comparable to the 256-distractor Experiment 03 scenario.

risk_policy.objective: maximize confirmation recall, then precision, then stable method/config order

configuration.evidence_reuse: Only decision thresholds reuse evidence. Cache keys include ratio threshold, RANSAC threshold, and seed; changing any of them forces recomputation.

prior_exploratory_results.warning: Observed before configuration plumbing and calibration-distribution corrections; retained only as exploratory evidence and not used for final selection.

timing.scope: feature extraction, calibration, evaluation, diagnostics and hashing

memory.scope: process-lifetime Linux ru_maxrss including native OpenCV allocations

limitations: A plausible homography is correspondence evidence, never proof of duplicate identity.
Natural negatives use Copydays identity and nearest-pHash hard-pair selection.
The held-out Strong identities were previously observed in Experiment 03 reporting.
Final and calibration databases use disjoint halves of the available distractors; each is smaller than the Experiment 03 target database.
Threshold search is small; Wilson intervals do not model identity clustering.
ORB exhaustive matching cost is not representative of an indexed production system.

implementation_review: configuration values reach homography plausibility checks
evidence cache key covers all evidence-changing configuration
calibration and evaluation query identities and distractors are disjoint
legacy Experiment 03 baseline retained as exploratory evidence
